description: Public-sector control schema for the CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework. Scoped to U.S. federal civilian agencies (FCEB). Maps SRF layers and accountable personas to OMB M-25-21 minimum practices, OMB M-25-22 acquisition requirements, FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators, NIST AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile), NIST COSAiS overlays (draft), and OWASP LLM Top 10. Each control carries a responsibility_split value aligned to FedRAMP Customer Responsibility Matrix categories.
regulatory_context: OMB M-25-21 (April 3, 2025) requires federal civilian agencies to apply seven minimum risk management practices to every high-impact AI use case and report compliance to OMB by September 22, 2026. Use cases that cannot meet the minimum practices must be discontinued. FedRAMP 20x is moving AI services into agencies through machine-readable Key Security Indicators rather than point-in-time documents; the first AI 20x Low authorizations landed January 2026, OpenAI holds 20x Moderate, and IBM authorized 11 AI products including watsonx in April 2026. FedRAMP authorizes the CSP side only; this schema fills the agency side of the shared responsibility split for AI-specific obligations. OMB M-25-22 (April 2025) governs AI acquisition, data rights, vendor lock-in avoidance, and transparency requirements. NIST COSAiS overlays are still in draft; mappings to those overlays are marked TBD pending final publication.
mapping_status_note: M-25-21, M-25-22, and FedRAMP 20x KSI mappings verified against primary sources 2026-07-05 (memo texts and the machine-readable Consolidated Rules for 2026). COSAiS mappings remain TBD pending initial public drafts of the NISTIR 8605 overlays. Do not substitute invented IDs.

responsibility_split_values.csp: The cloud service provider (AI vendor) is solely responsible.
responsibility_split_values.shared: Responsibility is split between CSP and agency; both must implement assigned controls.
responsibility_split_values.inherited: The agency inherits this control from a FedRAMP-authorized CSP or interagency shared service; agency must verify inheritance is documented in the CRM.

Each entry must record the use case, operating component, point of contact, and whether the use case has been designated high-impact.

m_25_21_citation_format: M-25-21 citations use the form 'Section N(x)(y) (Title)' following the memo's implementation sections: Section 3 agency governance (3(a) roles and bodies, 3(b) responsible adoption, 3(c) federal bodies), Section 4 public trust (4(a) determining high-impact AI and waivers, 4(b)(i-vii) minimum risk management practices), Sections 5 and 6 high-impact definition and presumed categories. Verified against the memo text (whitehouse.gov, April 3, 2025) in July 2026. 'N/A' means no nexus.
m_25_22_citation_format: M-25-22 citations use the form 'Section N(x) (Title)': Section 3 agency-level requirements (3(c) privacy, 3(d) IP rights and government data), Section 4 acquisition lifecycle (4(a) requirements, 4(b) market research, 4(c) solicitation, 4(d) selection and award incl. 4(d)(iii) contract terms A-G, 4(e) administration, 4(f) closeout). Verified against the memo text (whitehouse.gov, April 3, 2025) in July 2026. 'N/A' means no nexus.
fedramp_20x_ksi_citation_format: FedRAMP 20x citations use Key Security Indicator IDs 'KSI-{FAMILY}-{INDICATOR}' with a statement gloss in parentheses, multiple citations separated by '; '. Verified against the machine-readable FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 (github.com/FedRAMP/rules) in July 2026; families CED, CMT, CNA, IAM, INR, MLA, PIY, RPL, SCR, SVC. 'N/A' means no KSI covers the control's subject.
